correctness.rationale: For each integer n≥1 the 3-row signed matching expansion is reconstructed by distinct-column inclusion--exclusion. The exact identity uses all seven sign moments. The matching count n³+2n+1 fixes parity. A four-column block with ΔC13=-4 and zero other moment changes preserves W when S2=-1; two zero bases and two -2 bases extend over all odd lengths. The all-eight sign block has zero seven nonconstant moments, preserving W universally; ±1 witnesses at lengths 2,4,6,8 extend over all even lengths. The null-frequency lower bound uses independent permutations within fixed distinct-column blocks. Fourier diagonalization gives the exact inverse/pseudoinverse ℓ² norms. A standalone integer FWHT on every matching supports all frequencies n=1..6; an independent matching DP exhausts all sign-column types n=7..12; finite checks are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: This identifies precisely when a canonical full-matching indicator on a three-row bipartite edge cube acts as an invertible convolution operator, and its exact least positive singular value for every width. It differs decisively from the earlier two-matching-only spectrum on the identical graph family (opposite outcomes at widths three and four). The explicit sign-moment blocks yield a structural parity mechanism and exponentially many null frequencies, rather than a mere unsigned matchings recount. Exact odd nullities and endpoint inverse norms are deliberately left open.
